papers.title: Using an Engineered Galvanic Redox System to Generate Positive Surface Potentials that Promote Osteogenic Functions.
papers.abstract: Successful osseointegration of orthopaedic and orthodontic implants is dependent on a competition between osteogenesis and bacterial contamination on the implant-tissue interface. Previously, by taking advantage of the highly interactive capabilities of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs), we effectively introduced an antimicrobial effect to metal implant materials using an AgNP/poly(dl-lactic- co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) coating. Although electrical forces have been shown to promote osteogenesis, creating practical materials and devices capable of harnessing these forces to induce bone regeneration remains challenging. Here, we applied galvanic reduction-oxidation (redox) principles to engineer a nanoscale galvanic redox system between AgNPs and 316L stainless steel alloy (316L-SA). Characterized by scanning electron microscopy , energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, atomic force microscopy, Kelvin probe force microscopy, and contact angle measurement, the surface properties of the yield AgNP/PLGA-coated 316L-SA (SNPSA) material presented a significantly increased positive surface potential, hydrophilicity, surface fractional polarity, and surface electron accepting/donating index. Importantly, in addition to its bactericidal property, SNPSA's surface demonstrated a novel osteogenic bioactivity by promoting peri-implant bone growth. This is the first report describing the conversion of a normally deleterious galvanic redox reaction into a biologically beneficial function on a biomedical metal material. Overall, this study details an innovative strategy to design multifunctional biomaterials using a controlled galvanic redox reaction, which has broad applications in material development and clinical practice.

summary_en.motivation: To harness electrical forces for promoting osteogenesis on orthopedic implants through a controlled galvanic redox system.
summary_en.method: A nanoscale galvanic redox system was engineered between silver nanoparticles and 316L stainless steel via a PLGA coating.

summary_en.validation: Surface properties were characterized by SEM, EDX, AFM, KPFM, and contact angle measurements, with in vitro osteogenesis assays.

papers.title: Bone remodelling of the proximal femur after total hip arthroplasty with 2 different hip implant designs: 15 years follow-up of the thrust plate prosthesis and the Bi-Metric stem
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The thrust plate prosthesis (TPP) was introduced to preserve bone in patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty. We assessed the long-term results of hip arthroplasty in patients who received the TPP compared to a traditional intramedullary stem (Bi-Metric). METHODS: In this prospective observational cohort study, we evaluated bone mineral density (BMD) using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), radiological imaging and clinical outcome using Harris Hip Score (HHS). Twenty patients received the TPP (group A) and 18 patients received the Bi-Metric stem (group B). Baseline was the 1st postoperative day, and subsequent follow-up was performed at 6 months, 1, 2, 8, 12 and 15 years after surgery. A four regions of interest (ROI) protocol was developed to assess BMD. RESULTS: In ROI1, bone resorption was significantly higher for group A at 6 months with a mean difference of 10% (95% confidence interval [CI], 4-16; p = 0.003) and 8% (95% CI, 1-15; p = 0.03) at 8 years. Regarding ROI4, group A had a lesser decrease in general compared to group B. The radiological findings did not reveal any subsidence or detectable implant migration. HHS improved from 53 (23-69) to 93 (55-100) in group A and from 51 (24-72) to 94 (78-100) in group B. CONCLUSION: The TPP was not found to be inferior to the Bi-Metric stem regarding bone preservation. The decrease in BMD in ROI4 was greater in group B. Clinical and radiological results also revealed that the TPP was not inferior to the Bi-Metric stem.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提供长期临床骨密度数据，可作为应力遮挡验证的背景参考，但无有限元建模或接触力学分析。
llm.why_not_core: No finite element modeling, no stress/strain quantification, no micromotion or contact mechanics analysis, and no patient-specific implant modeling.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估两种髋关节假体（TPP与Bi-Metric）长期骨保存效果。
summary_zh.method: 前瞻性队列研究，使用DXA测量骨密度并分组随访15年。
summary_zh.result: TPP在骨密度维持方面不劣于Bi-Metric，但ROI1处骨吸收早期更高。
summary_zh.validation: 临床DXA骨密度测量和Harris髋关节评分。

summary_en.motivation: To compare long-term bone preservation between the thrust plate prosthesis and a conventional intramedullary stem after total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A prospective observational cohort study with DXA-based BMD measurements at multiple follow-ups up to 15 years.
summary_en.result: The thrust plate prosthesis showed non-inferior bone preservation compared to the Bi-Metric stem, with greater BMD loss in ROI1 during early follow-up.
summary_en.validation: Clinical validation via dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry and Harris Hip Score.

papers.title: On Cracking and Microstructure of Ni-based Superalloy Inconel 738LC by Selective Laser Melting: The Influence of Processing Parameters

llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on cracking and microstructure of a high-temperature Ni-based superalloy for aerospace, with no biomedical implant context, no porous structure design for stress shielding, no fatigue testing for implants, and no surface characterization relevant to osseointegration.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究SLM工艺参数对镍基高温合金裂纹和微观结构的影响
summary_zh.method: 改变激光功率、扫描速度等参数进行SLM实验，结合微观表征
summary_zh.result: 发现工艺参数影响裂纹密度和微观组织，优化参数可减少裂纹

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the influence of selective laser melting processing parameters on cracking and microstructure of a Ni-based superalloy for aerospace applications.
summary_en.method: Conducted SLM experiments with varied laser power and scanning speed, followed by microstructural characterization using SEM and EBSD.
summary_en.result: Processing parameters significantly affect crack density and microstructure, with optimized parameters reducing crack formation.
summary_en.validation: Validation through microstructural analysis (SEM, EBSD) of as-built samples.
